title: Rapid and Furious
subtitle: It's time to cleanse anew, my darling.

items.text: A Nightmare at Green Lake
The young staff of the Foundation are making deductions from the current situation.
The city girl and the town girl lie on the sofa. They snuggle up to each other and fiddle with the clutter on the table.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Look, they are trying to solve the problem, yet we can do nothing but fiddle around.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Maybe I should have worked harder in college, so that I can at least understand a thing or two from the conversations.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Don't worry, Jennifer! I don't understand any of what they said either!

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: You are not alone. I'm here with you.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: I'm not like you. You literally don't know anything. I remember when we first met, you asked of everything I had on me.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: You grew up here, in a small town in the middle of nowhere. It is only normal that you don't know anything about the outside world.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: But I'm different. I've been to big cities, I've gone to college, I've read books, I pretended to be well-adapted to this lifestyle. But in fact, I'm still ignorant, knowing nothing but empty pleasures.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: My hair color gives away who I am. I'm a silly blondie.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Don't speak of yourself like this, Jennifer.
Anne sits up, frowning with anxiety. She raises her voice.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: You're not silly. You are smart! You make your own movie with a script you wrote by yourself!

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: You're pretty and kind, and you're the best person I've ever known. Please don't hate yourself.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Fine, I get it, but can you let go of my hand first? You're hurting me a bit.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Oh! Sorry! Are you going to be okay? Shall I get you some ointment for these red areas on your hand?

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Haha! You're funny. I'm not some glass doll that breaks for being held too tightly.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Heh heh. Oh, I can barely breathe. You are great fun!

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: You're smiling. Did I make you happy? This is good.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Heh heh. Don't you find me weird?

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: My attitude changes so rapidly. I've been mean to you for a long time. And all of a sudden, I started to follow you around and try to use you to survive from this.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Weird? What's so bad about that?

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Even if you're weird, it's a good kind of weird. I like you ... staying by my side.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Even if I'm a benefit-driven fence-sitter who immediately embraced arcanists after being ditched by my human friends?

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Jason and Michael shouldn't hate you, if they knew you better.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Hah ...
The laughter makes her tired. She lets her body fall on the sofa, her head leaning on the shoulder of that small-town girl.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: You seem to really like me.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: You would jump off the car to rescue me, you protect me, praise me. You would even be happy because I was happy.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Because I've never seen anyone as pretty as you are.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: You're special. You're different to the rest of us.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Oh, stop. I will not be embarrassed for these nice things you said about me. I've heard enough of them throughout my entire life.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Listen. I'm very sorry for mistreating you, and I'm grateful that you came to save me.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: I will reward you with a secret, my secret. Do you wanna hear it?

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: Absolutely!
Anne's green eyes are filled with sincerity, shining like a puppy's.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: I'd love to!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: In fact, I don't hate horror movies.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: This is the diary I found in the attic. There were many other things, like a full warehouse.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: I actually liked them a lot when I was a kid. I spent most of my time here, in Green Lake Campsite, writing my own horror movie scripts on paper.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: The handwriting is pretty childish, so the writer might be around 8 to 13 years old. Some of the narratives are straightforward, but the story itself is very creative.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: But later, we moved to another town.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Huh, hah! My parents earned great success in business, and we moved into a high-profile community where only humans are allowed. We were also given privileges that arcanists cannot enjoy.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: It was then I realized—nobody wants me to be an arcanist.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It was since that day, the diary stopped updating.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It might be forgotten or taken away. The story ended there.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: That's why I decided to break off my connections with arcanists and stop showing interests in emotive things like horror movies in order to hide the arcanist side of me.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Huh! I took out my energy on other things which may ease my mind, like soap operas, new clothes, fashions ...

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: People like me this way. They said this is what I'm supposed to do.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: They believe that I'm a dumb bimbo, believe that I hate books. I led a life they want me to have, till I graduated from high school.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: I don't like these people.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: You shouldn't have been put through this. You are the smartest person I've ever known.
Anne reaches out a hand and clenches a fist.

items.speaker: Anne
items.text: If one day I run into them, I will pull their noses and mouths off, like this!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: A wonderful idea. I wish I was as creative as you are.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: So, in the end, I attacked one of the jerks who didn't watch his mouth at the prom.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: I slapped him in the face and smashed four sandwiches and a salad on his head.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Then, feeling resentful for what had happened, I applied for a degree in filmmaking, a course which was considered to be "ill-fitted" to me. And next, I started shooting horror movies for an assignment "I have to finish."

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Huh! Deep down inside, I think I have never really given them up. I've probably never stopped loving them.

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Keep on shooting. I will buy you a new camera.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Hello! Have you been eavesdropping? Where is your manners?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Actually, I heard them all as well.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: So did I.

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: We are in the same room. You can talk, we can hear, and the air helps. That's it.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Well, we are all here, paying attention to your voices. We heard everything you just said.
Tooth Fairy walks up, gently putting a pink diary on Blonney's knees.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I think this is yours. Now I should hand it back to you.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Where did you find it? I haven't seen this for a really long time.
A reunion after a long separation. Blonney opens the diary carefully.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: I used to do some arcanist tricks with it, but I have lost control over my power since I threw it into the la- … lak- ... Aaah-choo!
Blonney suddenly gives a shiver, perhaps because she is touched by the diary, or perhaps because of something else.
She raises her head and looks around.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Aren't you guys cold? How come it's so chilly?
A gust of cold wind, along with a bit of rain, swirls into the cabin. Outside the opened door, a wedding ring lies in a puddle, reflecting light ominously.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: That ring? Wasn't it on my finger a minute ago?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Watch out! Something is approaching.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: How many more dead men were buried here? I've had enough!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Can't we just get rid of that dead woman?

items.speaker: Ghost Bride
items.text: Boohoo …

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: She's approaching! This is a good chance ...

items.speaker: Ghost Bride
items.text: Aaahhh!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Ugh! She smells like a skunk in the sewer!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Blonney! The ghost bride took her down. We need to help her!

items.speaker: Critter Crowd
items.text: Squeak …

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Not good. The critters are coming around again!
The ghost bride murmurs something and crawls over Blonney, who has fallen to the ground.

items.speaker: Ghost Bride
items.text: I do ... do ... I do ... ah ...

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Hey! Blondie! If you wanna survive, leave that ring alone!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Hell, you think I wanted this?! This crazy woman ghost put it on me!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Get off! Get lost!
The ghost bride's oozy body is kicked back several feet.

items.speaker: Ghost Bride
items.text: Uuuhh ...!
Blonney quickly struggles to her feet and runs toward the back of the cabin.

items.speaker: Ghost Bride
items.text: Hmm, boohoo … uuhh ...

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Damn! Her whimper can summon more critters. They are going out from the ground!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Shh.
Shaking her head, Tooth Fairy walks to the center of the monsters.
She is surrounded by sparkling powder.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What they need is a song.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This is Ms. Tooth Fairy's singing!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, behind you!

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Jeez! What on earth is that!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Ahahaha! What is it, do you think?

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Of course, a good surpriiiiiiiiise!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Ha! I didn't know I was a talented driver!

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Once we get out of here, I'm gonna get myself a driver's license!

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Within 30 seconds, you crashed over every critter in our sight. I don't think you are qualified to be a driver.

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: No, no. That's not the point. Where did you get the car?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Pink lines. This is drawn with an oil paint pen. This is her arcane skill.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Your arcane skill restored pretty fast. Seems like you've accepted your identity.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Maybe that, or maybe because I retrieved this diary. I feel something has changed inside me, making me a bit hyped.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: A good try. Please keep up with the feeling.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: That song you just sang—can I take it as a gift?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You mean ...?

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Well, you still owe me a song. Please, I wanna a song from you.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Sure, take it as a gift.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: For making progress in life and for your courage to embrace who you truly are.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: Thanks.

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: This is my handkerchief. Take it. Wipe your face. Ah!
The Hummer woven with pink graffiti horns and melts in the rain. Blonney stumbles backward.
It's a misjudgment of her own arcane ability—a mistake commonly made by rookie arcanists.

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Did you just get a bit woozy from putting up a big scene to the rescue?

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: I didn't.

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: Okay … uh-huh … yeah … uh-hum ...

items.speaker: Blonney
items.text: What are you doing?

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: I know the rules of social courtesy. You just saved my life, so I won't embarrass you by telling others you just overestimated your ability.
Horropedia shakes his hand, a grin spreading across his face.

items.speaker: Horropedia
items.text: If you are willing to take advice from me, I would say don't overburden yourself.
